plugin_sdk_settings.url.description: Base HTTP or HTTPS URL of the OpenTSDB server, including its port. The plugin appends the API path.

plugin_sdk_settings.keepCookies.description: Cookie names Grafana passes to the plugin. The OpenTSDB backend HTTP client does not forward those cookies to the server.

plugin_sdk_settings.basicAuth.description: Enable this only when the OpenTSDB endpoint requires HTTP Basic authentication. It defaults to false. TLS settings and custom HTTP headers work independently of Basic auth.

plugin_sdk_settings.tlsAuthWithCACert.description: Verify the server certificate with a custom certificate authority.

plugin_sdk_settings.tlsCACert.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate used to verify the server.

plugin_sdk_settings.tlsSkipVerify.description: Skip verification of the OpenTSDB server certificate and hostname.

plugin_sdk_settings.serverName.description: Optional hostname used for TLS certificate verification and SNI. The editor shows it with TLS Client Auth. Provisioning also accepts it with a custom CA alone.

plugin_sdk_settings.withCredentials.description: Sets the credentials flag on legacy browser HTTP requests. Backend queries use the plugin HTTP client.

plugin_sdk_settings.oauthPassThru.description: Pass the signed-in user's OAuth identity from Grafana to the plugin. The OpenTSDB backend HTTP client does not forward it to the server.

plugin_sdk_settings.basicAuthUser.description: Username to send when HTTP Basic authentication is enabled. Omit it for connections without Basic auth.

plugin_sdk_settings.basicAuthPassword.description: Password to send when HTTP Basic authentication is enabled. Omit it for connections without Basic auth.

fields.label: Access
fields.description: Grafana provisioning defaults to proxy access. The editor has no access selector and plugin queries run on the backend.

fields.label: Timeout
fields.description: HTTP request timeout in whole seconds. Zero removes the request timeout.

fields.label: Custom HTTP Headers
fields.description: Extra HTTP headers sent to OpenTSDB. Provision each name as jsonData.httpHeaderName1, httpHeaderName2, and so on. Store each matching value in secureJsonData.httpHeaderValue1, httpHeaderValue2, and so on.

validations.message: Use a valid HTTP header name.

fields.label: Version
fields.description: Select the OpenTSDB release to set query editor features and the response format. Use 1 for 2.1 or earlier, 2 for 2.2, 3 for 2.3, or 4 for 2.4.

fields.label: Resolution
fields.description: The editor stores 1 for seconds or 2 for milliseconds. This setting has no effect on current queries, which request and read timestamps in seconds.

fields.label: Lookup limit
fields.description: Maximum results for suggestions and tag-value lookups, as a nonnegative whole number. Zero or an omitted limit sends 1000 for suggestions and 0 for tag-value lookups. Set 1000 explicitly to use it for both. Tag-key lookups always request 1000.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Route requests through the secure SOCKS proxy configured on the Grafana instance. In Grafana Cloud, set secureSocksProxyUsername to the selected PDC private network ID.

fields.label: Proxy username
fields.description: In Grafana Cloud, supply the selected PDC private network ID. For a self-managed SOCKS proxy, supply its username or omit it to use the data source UID.

fields.label: Proxy password
fields.description: Password for a self-managed SOCKS proxy if it requires one.

fields.label: Proxy keep-alive
fields.description: TCP keep-alive interval in whole seconds for the SOCKS proxy connection. Zero uses the Go dialer default. A negative value disables keep-alive probes.

instructions.msg: In provisioning YAML, write custom header names to jsonData.httpHeaderName1 and subsequent consecutive indexes. Write each value only to secureJsonData.httpHeaderValue1 with the same index. For a v0alpha1 resource use spec.jsonData.httpHeaderName1 and secure.httpHeaderValue1.create.

Leave Basic auth disabled and omit basicAuthUser and secureJsonData.basicAuthPassword unless the requested connection uses Basic auth. When enabled, supply the username and password that the server accepts.
